deepdive.sec: Affordable Private Hospital Chains / North India Cluster

bull_bear.body: Debt repayment priority (INR 28cr outstanding to be cleared); Organic growth (Greenfield/Brownfield); Opportunistic acquisitions of distressed assets; No dividend mentioned, focus on reinvestment for capacity doubling.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Execution risk on rapid capacity addition (1,500 beds in 2 years); Regulatory changes in CGHS/insurance rates beyond current hike; Talent acquisition for new units; Integration risks in acquired distressed assets.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident; Emphasis on 'capital efficiency', 'affordable healthcare', and 'operational discipline'; Transparent on CGHS benefits and receivable improvements (Debtor days down to 129 from 161).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management explicitly reframes ARPOB analysis, arguing expenses should be benchmarked to total revenue per bed-count rather than ARPOB alone, highlighting their high-volume/low-cost model vs. premium competitors; Bathinda unit turned PAT positive in month one of acquisition, defying typical turnaround timelines.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet described as "Negative Net Debt with comfortable leverage position", with "Strong liquidity with Rs 2,998 mn in FDs" and "Significant headroom to raise debt for future growth".
- Stated philosophy of disciplined capital allocation: "Focus on ROCE-accretive expansion opportunities", a "Track record of efficient capital deployment" and "Continuous evaluation of new growth avenues".
- Inorganic track record of 11 hospitals successfully acquired and integrated for cumulative consideration paid of Rs 9,991 Mn, adding 2,840 beds; individual considerations range from Rs 110 Mn for Faridabad (150 beds, Jan 2014) to Rs 2,450 Mn for KP Institute of Medical Sciences, Agra (360 beds, Feb 2026).
- Equity optionality flagged: promoter holding at ~82.9% with "Headroom for dilution up to regulatory threshold (~75%)", providing "flexibility for future equity raise if required".
- Rudrapur structure: acquired at a valuation of INR 1,770 mn with consideration paid for 80% ownership of INR 1,416 mn, and the remaining 20% to be acquired by FY'30.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: High-end specialties (Cardio, Onco, Neuro, Ortho) now 56.9% of revenue (+316 bps YoY); Oncology revenue share grew to 6.5% (FY26) from 5% (FY25); 150+ kidney transplants, 4,700+ PTCA, 2,600+ robotic joint replacements performed in FY26.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Competitors in North India facing higher capex intensity and slower occupancy ramp in Tier-2 cities. | Narayana Health | beneficiary | Med | Park's aggressive pricing and CGHS dominance may pressure margins of peers with higher cost structures in overlapping geographies. |
| Distressed hospital assets in North India requiring turnaround expertise. | Global Health Ltd (Medanta) | beneficiary | Low | While Medanta focuses on premium, Park's success in turning around distressed assets could tighten competition for acquisition targets in the region. |
| Vendors of medical consumables facing intense price negotiation from high-volume chains. | Medical Device Distributors (Unlisted) | loser | High | Management highlighted 'prolonged joint meetings' and 'low negotiated rates' with vendors to offset oncology drug price caps, squeezing distributor margins. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Described as the "Largest Private Hospital Chain in Haryana & Tricity" and "Second Largest in North India", with 17 hospitals across 15 cities in 6 states and 30+ super-speciality & speciality services.
- Growth and operating model is explicitly cluster-based - "Cluster based approach leveraging the benefits of proximity between hospitals" and "Cluster Format For Capex & Opex Efficiency".
- Accreditation base of 16 NABH accredited hospitals and 9 NABL & NABH accredited, with the recently opened Panchkula facility undergoing NABH accreditation and labs in 4 additional hospitals planned for NABL.
- Doctor-led professional management under promoters Dr. Ajit Gupta (Chairman and Whole Time Director, 44 years registered with MCI/NMC) and Dr. Ankit Gupta (Managing Director), who established Park Hospital, New Delhi in 2005; supported by a senior team spanning CEO, CFO, COO and Group Medical Director.
- Payor breadth spans government schemes and PSU (ESIC, CGHS, ECHS, Ayushman Bharat/PMJAY), TPA-linked cashless and direct insurance billing, and self-pay from the "Cash-pay middle & lower-middle income segment".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Contradiction - Rudrapur] The MD's letter describes "a definitive agreement to acquire 100% of 'The Medicity Hospital' in Rudrapur ... in an all-cash transaction valued at INR 177 crores", while the acquisitions-slide footnote states it "was acquired at a valuation of INR 1,770 mn (consideration paid for 80% ownership is INR 1,416 mn) ... Remaining 20% to be acquired by FY'30". Both readings are carried as printed.
- [Acquisition] The 200-bed hospital in Narela, Delhi was "acquired through the insolvency process" and "remains on track", slated for Dec 2026.
- [Listing / ownership] Shareholding as on 30-06-2026: Promoter & Promoter Group 82.9%, Institutions 9.8%, Non Institutions 7.3%; top institutional holders named as Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund, Abakkus Asset Management, Carnelian Asset Management and SBI General Insurance. Share performance is shown from 17 December 2025 to 31 July 2026 with Park at +80.6%, against index moves of +9.7%, -0.5%, -5.7%, +20.1% and +14.6%.
- [Industry] Healthcare delivery segment growing at ~10-12% CAGR (FY'24-FY'29P) with the market moving from INR 3.9 tn and INR 6.3 tn to INR 6.9-7.0 tn and INR 10.2-10.8 tn; ~3 Mn beds required to bridge the demand-supply gap; India average bed density ~15 beds per 10,000 population versus a global average of ~33 and an NHP recommendation of 20; North India's market share is expected to grow the fastest and Tier 2/Tier 3 demand is growing at around 16% to 18% CAGR.
- [Policy tailwind] Cited drivers include a CGHS rate revision of ~10-15%, Ayushman Bharat with 40+ Cr cards and 9+ Cr hospitalizations, digital health (ABHA) for faster claims, and health insurance penetration expected to rise from 40-42% (FY'24) to 45-50% (FY'27E), with insured people up from 288 Mn (2014-15) to 573 Mn (2023-24).
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Q4 margin expansion (268 bps) driven by high occupancy and operating leverage in existing units; Greenfield units (Panchkula) expected to reach EBITDA breakeven in 12-15 months; Brownfield units (Bathinda, Agra) achieved PAT positivity within first month/year; Vendor negotiations mitigated oncology drug cost pressures.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: 7-7.5% appreciation in FY27 from CGHS hike (9-month impact); Margins: Expected to hold/expand despite Greenfield ramp (Panchkula) due to CGHS benefits and high occupancy in new Brownfield units; Order Inflow: Occupancy ramping at 65-70% for Bathinda, INR 5cr/month run-rate for Agra; Capex: INR 500cr planned over next 2 years for 1,500 new beds.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: 1,500 beds under execution (Panchkula commissioned, Mohali expansion, Rohtak, Kanpur, Gorakhpur planned); Target capacity 5,460 beds by March 2028.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Uttar Pradesh expansion (0 to 1,060 beds by FY28 via Agra, Kanpur, Gorakhpur clusters); Tri-City dominance with Panchkula + Mohali expansion (850 beds); Ambala oncology extension; Potential for further distressed asset acquisitions in North India.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Park Medi World delivered record FY26 performance with 21% revenue growth and 26% EBITDA margins, driven by a 20% bed capacity addition and operational leverage, while positioning itself as the primary beneficiary of the 12-15% CGHS rate hike expected to flow through in FY27. The company's debt-free balance sheet and rapid integration of distressed assets (Bathinda, Agra) validate a capital-efficient expansion model targeting 5,460 beds by FY28.

drhp.business: Park Medi World operates a network of 14 NABH-accredited multi-super-specialty hospitals across Haryana, New Delhi, Punjab and Rajasthan under the 'Park' brand, offering over 30 super-specialty and specialty services. It serves largely lower-middle and middle-class patients, with revenue heavily weighted to government schemes/PSUs, and has grown through a cluster-based mix of organic build-out and hospital acquisitions.

Ambala expanding from 250 to 450 beds plus onco-radiation (operational by Oct 2027); Panchkula 300-bed hospital (by Apr 2026); Rohtak 250-bed hospital (by Dec 2026); Gorakhpur 400-bed O&M hospital (by Apr 2026); Kanpur 300-bed hospital under renovation (by Apr 2026). Company expects total bed capacity to rise to 4,900 beds by March 31, 2028.

Acquired Park Hospital, Palam Vihar (Rs 1,075.00 million) and Nidaan Hospital, Sonipat (Rs 520.00 million)
Acquired Grecian Super Speciality Hospital, Mohali (Rs 2,250.00 million)
Converted to public limited company and renamed Park Medi World Limited; entered Gorakhpur O&M agreement
Acquired 55% of Devina Derma (Kanpur hospital); commenced Krishna Super Speciality Hospital, Bhatinda; NCLT approved Durha Vitrak/Febris resolution plan

overview.one_liner: Second largest private hospital chain in North India and largest in Haryana by bed capacity, operating 14 NABH-accredited multi-super-specialty hospitals under the 'Park' brand.
verdict_pointers: Promoters hold 95.55% pre-Offer; only two shareholders above 1%
Fresh Issue Rs 7,700 million; Offer for Sale Rs 1,500 million by Promoter Dr. Ajit Gupta
Majority of Net Proceeds (Rs 3,800 million) earmarked for debt repayment

compliance_legal.evidence: Absolute RPTs Rs 468.83M, Rs 578.19M, Rs 918.32M, Rs 1,779.39M, Rs 2,154.66M = 5.80%, 8.36%, 6.59%, 14.45%, 17.17% of revenue; KMP salaries Dr. Ajit/Ankit Gupta Rs 294.00M each FY2025
compliance_legal.title: Related party transactions and conflicts of interest

compliance_legal.detail: Intensive Softshare (promoter group of BRLM Intensive Fiscal Services) holds shares, creating perceived conflict.
compliance_legal.evidence: Intensive Softshare holds 1,325,835 Equity Shares (0.34%); Dr. Ankit Gupta transferred 530,334 shares at Rs 471.40; Rajeev Jain holds 1,877,500 shares (0.49%)
compliance_legal.title: BRLM cross-shareholding / conflict of interest

compliance_legal.detail: Company, subsidiaries, promoters, directors and management face pending proceedings; adverse outcomes could hurt.
compliance_legal.evidence: Aggregate amounts: Against Company Rs 44.03M; Against Subsidiaries Rs 1,300.91M; Against Directors Rs 6.37M; Against Promoters Rs 6.37M; RoC adjudication penalty Rs 37,000 each (paid, closed)
compliance_legal.title: Outstanding legal and regulatory proceedings

compliance_legal.detail: Heavily regulated; failure to obtain/renew approvals or maintain NABL/NABH accreditations could halt operations.
compliance_legal.evidence: Blood bank license renewals applied for Park Hospital New Delhi (July 9, 2025) and Palam Vihar (Jan 27, 2025); NABL for 8 hospitals, NABH for all
compliance_legal.title: Approvals, licenses, registrations, permits and accreditations

compliance_legal.detail: Exposed to medical negligence claims, criminal/civil consequences and possible removal from Medical Register.
compliance_legal.evidence: Subsidiary Park Medicity North and Promoters party to an alleged medical-negligence matter (criminal litigation, p.486)
compliance_legal.title: Medical negligence and healthcare-service claims

compliance_legal.detail: Non-compliance with safety, health, environmental and employment laws could trigger penalties or shutdowns.
compliance_legal.evidence: Subject to inspections; no material non-compliance stated in H1 FY26/last three Fiscals
compliance_legal.title: Safety/health/environmental and labour compliance

compliance_legal.detail: Past delays/defaults in statutory dues could invite regulatory action and penalties.
compliance_legal.evidence: Delays: TDS Rs 11.19M (H1 FY26), EPF Rs 1.17M, ESIC Rs 0.88M; defaults incl. PMWL TDS Rs 0.96M, Kailash ESIC Rs 1.09M / EPF Rs 0.08M
compliance_legal.title: Delayed statutory dues

compliance_legal.detail: Key trademarks/logos ('Park', 'Park Hospital', 'The Signature') registered to Promoter Dr. Ajit Gupta, used via NOCs with no formal agreement.
compliance_legal.evidence: Five trademarks; NOCs dated Aug 29, 2022, Oct 12, 2011, Nov 26, 2019; no royalty and no agreements
compliance_legal.title: IP registered in Promoter's name

compliance_legal.detail: Healthcare price capping and reimbursement policy changes could reduce revenue and margins.
compliance_legal.evidence: Past impact from CGHS pricing adoption, NPPA implant price caps, COVID fixed pricing
compliance_legal.title: Regulatory reforms and pharmaceutical pricing

compliance_legal.detail: If states impose subsidized pricing or free beds, margins and pricing flexibility could suffer.
compliance_legal.evidence: Currently not subject to such obligations
compliance_legal.title: State-mandated subsidized/free healthcare

compliance_legal.detail: Failure of internal controls, fraud or AML/anti-corruption non-compliance could impose penalties.
compliance_legal.evidence: Periodic inspections by AERB, Fire & Safety, NABH; no adverse findings stated
compliance_legal.title: Employee misconduct / internal controls / anti-corruption

compliance_legal.detail: Promoters retain majority control and can influence all shareholder matters, potentially conflicting with minority interests.
compliance_legal.evidence: Promoters hold 95.55% of paid-up equity share capital as on RHP date
compliance_legal.title: Promoter control after the Offer

compliance_legal.detail: Related-party interests via directorships, shareholding, leases and trademark usage.
compliance_legal.evidence: Delhi hospital lease Rs 1.2M/Rs 0.6M/month to promoters; Ratangiri O&M with Shri Amar Charitable Trust and Girdhari Lal Saini Memorial Health Society (Promoter Group); Dr. Ajit Gupta holds 18.19% of Park Medicenters
compliance_legal.title: Promoters/Directors/KMP interested beyond remuneration

compliance_legal.detail: Acquisition-driven strategy exposes Company to Competition Act/CCI scrutiny and penalties.
compliance_legal.evidence: Competition (Amendment) Act 2023 reduced combination review to 150 days and enables global-turnover-based penalties
compliance_legal.title: Competition law exposure

compliance_legal.detail: Evolving laws (GST on consumables, new Labour Codes, DPDP Act, new criminal codes) create compliance and liability risk.
compliance_legal.evidence: Labour Codes effective Nov 21, 2025; DPDP Rules notified Nov 13, 2025; ambiguity on GST for in-patient medicines/consumables
compliance_legal.title: Changing laws / tax / GST / labour codes / data protection

compliance_legal.detail: Investors may be unable to enforce foreign judgments except by fresh suit in India.
compliance_legal.evidence: Sections 13 and 44A CPC; India lacks reciprocity with, e.g., the United States
compliance_legal.title: Enforcement of foreign judgments against Company/management

compliance_legal.detail: FDI/FEMA restrictions (incl. Press Note 3) limit ability to attract foreign investors.
compliance_legal.evidence: Press Note No. 3 (2020) requires prior GoI approval for land-border-country investments
compliance_legal.title: Foreign investment restrictions

compliance_legal.detail: Takeover Regulations may deter a change of control even at a premium.
compliance_legal.evidence: SEBI Takeover Regulations define acquirer and may discourage third-party takeover
compliance_legal.title: Anti-takeover provisions under Indian law

compliance_legal.detail: Foreign investors may be unable to exercise pre-emptive rights, suffering dilution.
compliance_legal.evidence: Companies Act pre-emptive rights may require Company to file registration statement in investor's jurisdiction
compliance_legal.title: Restricted pre-emptive rights

financial_valuation.detail: Significant contingent liabilities and corporate guarantees relative to net worth could materialize and hit financials.
financial_valuation.evidence: As of Sept 30, 2025 contingent liabilities (ex-corporate guarantees) = 11.66% of net worth; corporate guarantees = 71.58% of net worth; corporate guarantees to banks total Rs 7,493.33M; guarantee by subsidiary for Company Rs 760.00M
financial_valuation.title: Contingent liabilities and corporate guarantees

financial_valuation.detail: Multiple rating downgrades/withdrawals; further downgrades could raise borrowing costs and trigger covenants.
financial_valuation.evidence: CARE downgraded from CARE A- (Stable) to CARE BBB+ (Stable) Dec 12, 2024 then removed Jan 21, 2025; Brickwork downgraded BWR BBB to BWR BB- to BWR B+; current CRISIL A+ (Stable); RGS downgraded BWR BB to BWR BB-
financial_valuation.title: Credit rating downgrades

financial_valuation.detail: Revenue and restated PAT fell while material costs rose in FY2024 vs FY2023.
financial_valuation.evidence: Revenue -1.88% Rs 12,545.95M to Rs 12,310.66M; cost of materials +26.91% Rs 1,944.91M to Rs 2,468.33M; restated PAT -33.39% Rs 2,281.86M to Rs 1,520.07M
financial_valuation.title: Revenue and PAT decline in FY2024

financial_valuation.detail: Several subsidiaries incurred losses over the review period and may continue to.
financial_valuation.evidence: Park Medicity World losses Rs (43.24)M/Rs (89.78)M/Rs (119.45)M/Rs (145.00)M; RGS Rs (474.73)M FY2024; DMR Hospitals Rs (31.54)M FY2024; Kailash Rs (37.81)M FY2023
financial_valuation.title: Loss-making subsidiaries

financial_valuation.detail: Revenue concentrated in government schemes/PSUs with payment delays and claim rejections stretching working capital.
financial_valuation.evidence: Govt schemes/PSUs 83.38%-92.37% of revenue; claims disallowed Rs 945.10M (11.69%) H1 FY26, Rs 1,976.89M (15.76%) FY2023; trade receivable days 173.48; working capital cycle 151.40 days; trade receivables Rs 7,686.76M
financial_valuation.title: Delayed government/insurer payments and high receivables

financial_valuation.detail: Unconditional performance guarantees to ESIC/CGHS/ECHS could be invoked.
financial_valuation.evidence: As at Sept 30, 2025 performance guarantees amounted to Rs 73.05M
financial_valuation.title: Performance guarantees to government authorities

financial_valuation.detail: EBITDA, EBITDA margin, PAT margin, ROCE and EPS declined in FY2024.
financial_valuation.evidence: EBITDA Rs 3,903.41M(FY23) to Rs 3,103.01M(FY24); EBITDA margin 31.11% to 25.21%; PAT margin 18.19% to 12.35%; ROCE 26.78% to 16.07%; EPS Rs 5.94 to Rs 3.95
financial_valuation.title: Decline in key financial metrics in FY2024

financial_valuation.detail: Deployment of Net Proceeds rests on management estimates; delays/cost overruns possible.
financial_valuation.evidence: Objects of the Offer not appraised by any bank/financial institution; deployment schedule tied to Fiscal 2027
financial_valuation.title: Net Proceeds not independently appraised

financial_valuation.detail: Medical-equipment capex based on time-limited vendor quotations with no binding orders.
financial_valuation.evidence: Quotations valid for limited period; no definitive agreements to place equipment orders
financial_valuation.title: No definitive arrangements for part of Net Proceeds / vendor quotations

financial_valuation.detail: Outstanding debt with lender-consent covenants; breach could accelerate debt or trigger conversion to equity.
financial_valuation.evidence: Total outstanding borrowings Rs 6,243.11M (consolidated) as on Oct 31, 2025; prepayment penalties up to 2% (term/WC loans) and 4% (equipment loans)
financial_valuation.title: Borrowings and restrictive covenants

financial_valuation.detail: Unsecured loan repayable on demand could be recalled at any time.
financial_valuation.evidence: Unsecured loan from Healplus Labs Pvt Ltd: Rs 251.29M outstanding as on Sept 30, 2025; repayable on demand; 9.50% interest
financial_valuation.title: Recallable unsecured loan from group company

financial_valuation.detail: Multiple emphasis-of-matter notes on unconfirmed balances, related-party receivables and land/receivable realizability.
financial_valuation.evidence: FY2024 trade payables >3 years Rs 10.03M; RGS unconfirmed related-party loan Rs 161.73M; Rs 193.75M GMADA land reallotted to director; FY2023 receivables >1 year Rs 269.63M unsupported; Rs 48.99M director credit-card expenses without evidence; Park Medicenters payable Rs 226.73M
financial_valuation.title: Statutory Auditors' emphasis-of-matter observations

financial_valuation.detail: Professional fees/salaries to promoters rose in FY2025, an increased expense that may be unjustified if growth declines.
financial_valuation.evidence: Dr. Ajit Gupta salary Rs 294.00M FY2025; Dr. Ankit Gupta Rs 294.00M FY2025; professional fee Rs 6.00M each FY2025 vs Rs 4.80M FY2024
financial_valuation.title: Increased Promoter salaries in FY2025

financial_valuation.detail: Objects cannot be varied without special resolution; Company gets nothing from the Offer for Sale.
financial_valuation.evidence: Sections 13(8) and 27 Companies Act; Promoter Selling Shareholder receives entire OFS proceeds
financial_valuation.title: Variation of Net Proceeds requires approval; no OFS proceeds to Company

financial_valuation.detail: Post-listing quarterly results may vary and not reflect underlying performance.
financial_valuation.evidence: Fluctuations from expense timing, patient volumes, policy changes, pricing
financial_valuation.title: Quarterly results may fluctuate

financial_valuation.detail: Future dividends depend on earnings, working capital, capex and financing covenants.
financial_valuation.evidence: No dividend declared in H1 FY26 or last three Fiscals
financial_valuation.title: Dividend uncertainty

financial_valuation.detail: A downgrade could raise borrowing costs and impede financing.
financial_valuation.evidence: External macro risk; borrowing costs depend on India's sovereign ratings
financial_valuation.title: Sovereign credit rating downgrade of India

financial_valuation.detail: Global financial turmoil could increase Indian market volatility and restrict capital access.
financial_valuation.evidence: References to trade-war risk aversion and reduced global market liquidity
financial_valuation.title: Financial instability in other countries

financial_valuation.detail: Financials prepared under Ind-AS may not be comparable to other GAAPs.
financial_valuation.evidence: Significant differences exist between Ind-AS, U.S. GAAP and IFRS
financial_valuation.title: Ind-AS vs US GAAP/IFRS differences

financial_valuation.detail: EBITDA, margins, ROE/ROCE etc. are non-GAAP and may not be comparable across companies.
financial_valuation.evidence: Non-GAAP Measures not required by or presented under Ind AS/IFRS/US GAAP
financial_valuation.title: Non-GAAP measures not standardized

financial_valuation.detail: No prior public market; trading price may be volatile and Price Band may not indicate market price.
financial_valuation.evidence: Listed factors: quarterly variations, analyst recommendations, market conditions
financial_valuation.title: Equity share price volatility post-listing

financial_valuation.detail: Shares could be placed under ASM/GSM, imposing trading restrictions and higher margins.
financial_valuation.evidence: ASM/GSM parameters include price, P/E, delivery %, client concentration, volatility
financial_valuation.title: ASM/GSM surveillance measures

financial_valuation.detail: Investors subject to LTCG/STCG, STT, stamp duty and dividend taxes; law changes could affect returns.
financial_valuation.evidence: LTCG 10% above Rs 100,000 (Sec 112A); stamp duty 0.015% delivery / 0.003% non-delivery; Finance Act 2024 amended capital gains rates
financial_valuation.title: Indian capital gains and dividend taxes

financial_valuation.detail: Future issuances or major-shareholder sales could dilute holdings and depress price.
financial_valuation.evidence: Dilution via primary offering, convertibles, ESOPs; sales subject to SEBI ICDR lock-in
financial_valuation.title: Future equity issuance / dilution

financial_valuation.detail: Currency movements could reduce value/returns on Equity Shares for foreign investors independent of results.
financial_valuation.evidence: Dividends paid in Rupees and converted for repatriation
financial_valuation.title: Rupee exchange-rate fluctuation

financial_valuation.detail: Investors cannot sell immediately; delays in demat credit and trading approvals possible.
financial_valuation.evidence: Demat credit ~2 Working Days, trading ~3 Working Days from Bid Closing Date
financial_valuation.title: Listing/trading commencement delay

financial_valuation.detail: Offer Price may not indicate market price; some prior BRLM-managed issues trade below issue price.
financial_valuation.evidence: Price Band set via Book Building Process; current market price of certain past BRLM issues below issue price
financial_valuation.title: Price Band determination / past BRLM issues below issue price

financial_valuation.detail: QIBs and NIIs cannot withdraw/lower bids after submission despite adverse developments.
financial_valuation.evidence: Per SEBI ICDR Regulations; Retail can revise/withdraw until Bid/Offer Closing Date
financial_valuation.title: QIBs/NIIs cannot withdraw or lower bids

internal_operational.detail: Highly dependent on doctors, nurses and support staff amid limited supply of senior doctors; high attrition could impair service quality.
internal_operational.evidence: As of Sept 30, 2025 attrition rate of doctors was 33.72% (44.77% Sept 2024; 38.36%, 46.95%, 46.99% prior years); resident medical officer attrition 52.02%; team of 1,014 doctors, 2,142 nurses, 730 medical professionals, 2,025 support staff (562 consultants, 452 RMOs)
internal_operational.title: Doctor and staff attrition / dependence on medical professionals

internal_operational.detail: A large share of revenue comes from Haryana hospitals; regional slowdown, unrest or disasters would hit results.
internal_operational.evidence: Haryana contributed 69.06%, 74.62%, 73.43%, 76.92% and 83.91% of revenue from operations in H1 FY26, H1 FY25 and FY2025/2024/2023; network of 14 hospitals (8 in Haryana)
internal_operational.title: Geographic revenue concentration in Haryana

internal_operational.detail: Material/employee/consultancy costs are large and regulatory price caps limit pass-through.
internal_operational.evidence: Cost of materials + employee benefit + professional/consultancy fees were 64.10%, 66.57%, 67.26%, 60.97% and 57.27% of total expenses; total Rs 4,163.27M (H1 FY26)
internal_operational.title: High cost base and limited ability to pass costs to patients

internal_operational.detail: Many doctors work part-time under one-year consultancy agreements on a non-exclusive basis and could leave.
internal_operational.evidence: 562, 480, 527, 382, 339 consultants engaged; comprised 55.43%, 53.89%, 57.79%, 48.17%, 41.70% of total doctors; in H1 FY26 138 joined and 103 left
internal_operational.title: Reliance on consultancy-basis doctors

internal_operational.detail: Most revenue from seven specialties; obsolescence, price caps or demand shifts would hurt.
internal_operational.evidence: Internal medicine, neurology, urology, gastroenterology, cardiology, general surgery, orthopedics together contributed 86.13%, 92.18%, 88.34%, 92.87% and 92.42% of revenue; internal medicine alone 29.65%
internal_operational.title: Revenue concentration in a few key specialties

internal_operational.detail: Revenue heavily weighted to in-patients; occupancy fell sharply in FY2024 after Grecian acquisition.
internal_operational.evidence: In-patient operating income 94.89%-97.34% of revenue; bed occupancy 75.13% (FY2023) to 59.81% (FY2024) to 61.63% (FY2025); ARPOB lowest among listed peers per CRISIL; ALOS 6.35-6.97 days
internal_operational.title: Dependence on in-patient department and volatile bed occupancy

internal_operational.detail: Three hospitals on leased premises and two on revenue-share O&M agreements; disputes could end operations.
internal_operational.evidence: Owns 10 of operational hospitals; Amar Jaipur revenue share 1% of net sales or Rs 2.00M/month (cap Rs 2.30M); Krishna Bhatinda 15% of gross revenue; Gorakhpur 6.50% of receipts
internal_operational.title: Leased and revenue-share hospitals

internal_operational.detail: Park Hospital New Delhi land/floors and Registered Office leased from promoters on an 11-month term; non-renewal risks continuity.
internal_operational.evidence: 11-month lease w.e.f. March 10, 2025; rent Rs 1.2M/month to Dr. Ajit Gupta and Rs 0.60M/month to Dr. Ankit Gupta
internal_operational.title: Short-term lease of key Delhi hospital and Registered Office from Promoters

internal_operational.detail: Business depends on the 'Park' brand; negativity, malpractice or mortality events could erode trust.
internal_operational.evidence: Trademarks registered in name of Promoter Dr. Ajit Gupta; brand-dependence factors listed
internal_operational.title: Brand and reputation dependence

internal_operational.detail: Pharmacy, housekeeping, food, security, ICU services outsourced; termination or lapses create liability.
internal_operational.evidence: Material third-party expenses 22.95%, 25.33%, 25.05%, 21.06%, 20.53% of total expenses; pharmacy services alone 18.62% (Rs 1,209.6M); pharmacy via Plus Distribution Pvt Ltd
internal_operational.title: Reliance on third-party service providers

internal_operational.detail: Dependent on Hospital Management IT system; outages or breaches could disrupt care and trigger liability.
internal_operational.evidence: No stated instance of cyber breach in H1 FY26 or last three Fiscals, but risk of cyberattacks/data theft of medical data
internal_operational.title: IT systems and patient data security

internal_operational.detail: Expensive equipment evolves fast; failure to upgrade could reduce demand.
internal_operational.evidence: New medical equipment procurement 1.23%, 6.91%, 6.33%, 3.06%, 3.18% of total expenses; repair/maintenance upgrade 0.92%-1.13%
internal_operational.title: Technology / medical equipment obsolescence

internal_operational.detail: Most supplies bought on purchase-order basis from a concentrated vendor base.
internal_operational.evidence: Largest vendor was 40.14%, 44.57%, 42.40%, 46.09%, 45.68% of total purchases (Plus Distribution Pvt Ltd); third-party procurement spend Rs 1,479.34M-Rs 3,544.83M
internal_operational.title: Dependence on limited third-party vendors for supplies/equipment

internal_operational.detail: Loss of senior management or KMP without adequate replacement could harm the business.
internal_operational.evidence: No adverse resignation impact stated in H1 FY26/last three Fiscals but may need to raise compensation
internal_operational.title: Recruitment/retention of senior management and skilled personnel

internal_operational.detail: Operational beds are below total bed capacity; may fail to raise utilization.
internal_operational.evidence: Bed capacity 3,250 vs operational beds 3,050 (H1 FY26); capacity 3,000/3,000/2,900/2,550 vs operational 2,800/2,800/2,700/2,400
internal_operational.title: Underutilized bed capacity

internal_operational.detail: Hospitals susceptible to fire/floods; inflammable chemicals stored; insurance may not fully cover.
internal_operational.evidence: Severe Punjab floods in FY2024 briefly affected Healing Touch Ambala and Park Hospital Patiala
internal_operational.title: Fire, floods, natural and man-made disasters

internal_operational.detail: Failure or misuse of advanced (incl. radioactive) equipment could injure patients/staff and cause liability.
internal_operational.evidence: Repair and maintenance expense 1.31%, 1.64%, 1.59%, 1.62%, 1.41% of total expenses (Rs 85.31M H1 FY26)
internal_operational.title: Medical or other equipment failure/malfunction

internal_operational.detail: Manpower-intensive sector; unionization or stoppages could raise costs and disrupt services.
internal_operational.evidence: Presently none of hospital employees unionized; no major unrest in H1 FY26 or last three Fiscals
internal_operational.title: Labour unrest / unionization

internal_operational.detail: Insurance may not cover all risks including medical negligence claims; renewals uncertain.
internal_operational.evidence: Aggregate insurance coverage Rs 6,992.81M (Sept 30, 2025) = 102.66% of total assets (90%-102% across periods)
internal_operational.title: Insufficient insurance coverage

internal_operational.detail: A public-health crisis could divert patients, cause shutdowns, staffing shortages and price caps.
internal_operational.evidence: COVID-era price caps referenced; disaster plans and infectious-disease protocols in place
internal_operational.title: Pandemic / epidemic / infectious-disease outbreak

strategy_growth.detail: Track record of acquisitions; may fail to integrate or realize synergies and could inherit undisclosed liabilities.
strategy_growth.evidence: Acquired 8 hospitals in North India adding 1,650 beds as of Sept 30, 2025; Blue Heavens Durha Vitrak plan (Rs 483.01M to secured creditors + Rs 1.00M equity)
strategy_growth.title: Acquisition integration risk

strategy_growth.detail: Pipeline hospitals may not be built on time or reach anticipated operating capacity.
strategy_growth.evidence: Pipeline: Ambala (200 beds), Panchkula (300), Rohtak (250), Gorakhpur (400, O&M 30-yr), Kanpur (300); several 'construction yet to commence'
strategy_growth.title: Proposed hospital development pipeline

strategy_growth.detail: NCLT-approved resolution plan for Febris Multi Specialty Hospital is incomplete; benefits and integration unproven.
strategy_growth.evidence: Total payable Rs 483.41M; liquidation value Rs 339.94M; Febris 200-bed plan with 109 beds commissioned; Blue Heavens net asset value Rs 1,897.97M (Sept 30, 2025)
strategy_growth.title: Durha Vitrak / Febris (Blue Heavens) acquisition uncertainty

strategy_growth.detail: Delays/cost overruns or approval failures could stall the new hospital funded by Net Proceeds.
strategy_growth.evidence: Rs 605.00M from Net Proceeds toward New Hospital; total estimated cost Rs 812.23M; Fire/CTE/building-plan approvals received
strategy_growth.title: Rohtak New Hospital construction (Park Medicity NCR)

strategy_growth.detail: Need to sustain brand via marketing spend; failure to build brand could reduce patient inflow.
strategy_growth.evidence: Ad/business-promotion expense 0.88%, 1.25%, 1.48%, 0.64%, 0.83% of total expenses (Rs 57.33M H1 FY26)
strategy_growth.title: Advertisement and brand-promotion dependence

strategy_growth.detail: Faces larger and government hospitals plus telemedicine/AYUSH alternatives; may lose competitive edge.
strategy_growth.evidence: Company ~3,000 beds (0.13% market share) vs Apollo 10,187, Manipal 10,500, Max 5,100; ARPOB lowest among listed peers; ROE 11.64% H1 FY26 vs peers
strategy_growth.title: Competition from hospitals, pharmacies, diagnostics and telemedicine

strategy_growth.detail: New specialties may not generate expected demand or revenue.
strategy_growth.evidence: Programs launched incl. MAMBS and kidney transplant at Gurugram, Palam Vihar, The Signature
strategy_growth.title: Challenges launching new specialties/clinical programs

strategy_growth.detail: Industry/market information relies on a CRISIL Report commissioned and paid for by the Company.
strategy_growth.evidence: CRISIL Report dated Nov 2025, engagement letter Dec 20, 2024, exclusively commissioned and paid for by the Company
strategy_growth.title: Industry data commissioned and paid for by Company

strategy_growth.detail: India political/economic conditions, inflation, unrest and geopolitics beyond control could hurt operations.
strategy_growth.evidence: Lists political instability, civil unrest, inflation, forex reserve decline, interest-rate movements
strategy_growth.title: Broad political/economic macro factors

strategy_growth.detail: Sector-wide cost pressure, price caps and demographic shifts could adversely affect the business.
strategy_growth.evidence: Rising healthcare costs; possible GoI price/margin caps; poor infrastructure and paucity of specialized doctors per CRISIL
strategy_growth.title: Broader Indian healthcare-industry challenges

concerns_observed: Heavy geographic concentration in Haryana (73.43% of FY25 revenue) and payor concentration in government schemes/PSUs (88.46% of FY25 revenue)
Weak working capital profile: trade receivable days ~173 and working capital cycle ~151 days; claim disallowances of 11-16% of billings
FY24 setback: revenue -1.88%, restated PAT -33.39%, EBITDA margin 31.11% to 25.21%, EPS Rs 5.94 to Rs 3.95 after Grecian acquisition and occupancy fall to 59.81%
High off-balance-sheet exposure: corporate guarantees 71.58% of net worth; contingent liabilities (ex-guarantees) 11.66% of net worth

Governance/audit red flags: multiple emphasis-of-matter items (unconfirmed related-party balances, unsupported >1yr receivables, undocumented director credit-card expenses), key trademarks held personally by the promoter, and rating downgrades (CARE A- to BBB+ then withdrawn)

meta.thesis: Park Medi World delivered record FY26 performance with 21% revenue growth and 26% EBITDA margins, driven by a 20% bed capacity addition and operational leverage, while positioning itself as the primary beneficiary of the 12-15% CGHS rate hike expected to flow through in FY27. The company's debt-free balance sheet and rapid integration of distressed assets (Bathinda, Agra) validate a capital-efficient expansion model targeting 5,460 beds by FY28.
